abstract.t: This document is a subordinate specification of the PIC Specification 0.2. It defines the Causally Ordered Security-State (COSS) Evidence Record (CER): a protocol-neutral, transportable record that binds evidence from several security coordinates to one causal execution occurrence. COSS generalizes PIC from one authority coordinate to a finite product of ordered security coordinates while retaining PIC as the authority coordinate and preserving the foundational distinction between Proof of Relationship (PoR) and Proof of Continuity (PoC). A record may reference PIC authority-continuity evidence, information-flow evidence, execution-integrity evidence, geographic evidence, or other profile-defined evidence without absorbing the semantics of those systems.

The central rule is simple: one occurrence, one causal history, several independently verified coordinates. An authenticated digest reference proves that a record committed to exact artifact bytes; it does not prove that the referenced claim is true. Each required artifact remains subject to its own verifier, while the COSS record prevents valid evidence from unrelated executions from being mixed and presented as evidence of one effect.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: An effect can be authorized in one dimension and forbidden in another. A mail service may receive both a valid permission to send and bytes derived from confidential data. The permission answers what authority may continue. It does not answer where the bytes may flow.

COSS places those distinct security coordinates on the same causal execution [4]. This document specifies the evidence boundary needed to carry that relationship between systems. It does not define the internal semantics or wire format of PIC, information-flow control (IFC), runtime attestation, or any other coordinate.

section.name: Requirements Notation
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [2] [3] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

list.t: An occurrence is one represented security-relevant execution event.
Pred(e) is the set of represented immediate causal predecessors of occurrence e; Hist(e) is its represented causal history.
A coordinate is a profile-defined ordered security-state system with a state space, a "no more permissive than" order, admitted behaviors, evidence requirements, and a verifier.
K is the set of coordinate profiles required by trusted policy for a particular verification decision.
A COSS Evidence Record (CER) is authenticated witness material for one occurrence. It is not itself a verifier verdict.
A Producer creates a CER. A Verifier evaluates a CER and its predecessor graph under trusted policy.
A Profile supplies concrete representations, cryptographic mechanisms, coordinate semantics, and verification rules.
A transition class is root, ordinary, or authorized-relaxation.
An authorized relaxation is an explicitly authorized non-conservative coordinate transition. It is not an ordinary continuation.

A relaxation authority is a trust anchor or a delegated authority whose authorization path terminates at a trust anchor accepted by the Verifier. Its signature authenticates an authorization; the signature alone does not establish that the authorization is applicable.

section.name: Scope
section.t: This specification defines:

list.t: the logical contents of a COSS Evidence Record;
the binding of coordinate evidence to one execution occurrence and its causal predecessor set;
execution integrity as an optional security coordinate, distinct from the evidence system that realizes it;
the distinction between Proof of Possession (PoP), Proof of Relationship (PoR), and Proof of Continuity (PoC);
ordered verification of ordinary continuations, joins, and explicit authorized relaxations; and
the limits of digest references and external evidence.

section.t: This specification does not define a serialization, signature suite, transport, evidence-retention system, PIC representation, IFC model, or product-specific mapping. Profiles define those choices. A mapping to an execution-evidence system is a profile of this specification, not a redefinition of PIC or COSS semantics.

section.name: Relationship to PIC
section.t: COSS is the multi-coordinate generalization of PIC. PIC remains the authority coordinate and the source of the authority-specific PoR, PoC, and non-expansion semantics. COSS places that coordinate beside other independently defined ordered coordinates and requires all of them to refer to one causal occurrence and one predecessor graph. COSS does not replace PIC, and PIC continuity alone does not establish continuity for the complete COSS product.

section.name: Planned Companion Specifications
section.t: This document is standalone and defines the record model and the semantic conditions for COSS PoR and PoC. A future COSS Prover and Verifier Specification may define concrete proof production, recursive graph verification, verifier-result objects, error semantics, and protocol bindings. A separate future COSS-to-TRACE Profile may define a concrete TRACE mapping without making TRACE a dependency of COSS.

Those companion names describe planned work only. They do not identify published specifications, create conformance requirements, or alter the requirements of this document until separate documents are published and explicitly versioned.

section.name: One Effect, Several Questions
section.t: Alice authorizes reading her documents for a verification. Bob independently authorizes sending official email. Carol is an AI agent; in the accepted variant below, Carol acts as a Data Loss Prevention (DLP) service. Trent stores Alice's documents. Dave is a mail service whose rule forbids confidential data over email.

figure.artwork:
Alice -- read for verification --\ \ Bob -- send official email ------> Carol / Trent -- documents; HIGH --------/ | | send(bytes) v Dave
Dave's rule: no confidential data by email

section.t: The two permissions can be individually valid while the proposed effect remains inadmissible. Dave receives a permission and bytes:

figure.artwork:
send request permission: send email bytes: 52 65 6c 61 7a 69 6f 6e 65 ...
authority question: may this occurrence send email? flow question: may these bytes flow to this destination? causal question: which earlier occurrences produced this request and these bytes?

section.t: Neither the bytes nor the send permission answers all three questions. A log entry with an actor and timestamp does not establish the causal relationship. Evidence is sufficient for this effect only when the relevant answers are bound to the same occurrence.

section.name: One Causal Axis
section.t: Let e be an execution occurrence and Pred(e) its represented immediate causal predecessors. Its represented history is the causal down-set Hist(e), not a wall-clock interval and not a second timeline per security mechanism [4] [7].

figure.artwork: Alice intent --> Trent release --\ > Carol send Bob intent ----------------------/ | v Dave effect

section.t: Common ancestry, equal timestamps, the same executor, or co-residence in one process MUST NOT be treated as proof that two branches are the same continuation. A claimed predecessor edge requires profile-defined, causally sound evidence.

section.name: COSS Security State
section.t: For a finite set of coordinate profiles J, the security state at occurrence e is:

figure.artwork: Sigma(e) = (sigma_j(e)) for every j in J

section.t: Each profile j defines:

list.t: its state space;
its order <=_j, meaning "no more permissive than";
the behaviors admitted by a state; and
the evidence and verification procedure that establish its claims.

section.t: For states x' and x, every conformant coordinate profile MUST make its order semantically monotone:

figure.artwork: x' <=_j x implies admitted_j(x') subset-of admitted_j(x)

section.t: The profile MUST justify this implication for its concrete state representation and behavior semantics. It MUST NOT infer semantic monotonicity merely from a syntactic ordering or from proofs about a different coordinate. This is a profile proof obligation; it is not inherited automatically from a PIC implementation or from the formal proofs for another state space [4].
For an ordinary causal edge p -> e, COSS continuity requires:

figure.artwork: PoR_COSS(p, e) AND sigma_j(e) <=_j sigma_j(p) for every required j

section.t: PIC is the authority coordinate of this construction. For set-valued PIC authority C, the order is set inclusion:

figure.artwork: PoR_COSS(p, e) AND C(e) subset-of C(p)

section.t: An IFC profile may provide a different state and order. COSS does not require distinct coordinates to use the same vocabulary, verifier, or artifact format. It requires their results to constrain the same occurrence.

If a coordinate translates between heterogeneous state spaces, the profile MUST define the translation, prove that it is monotone in the source and target orders, and state the semantic relation preserved across their behavior universes. A translation that is order-preserving but excessively permissive in its intended security meaning is a profile or deployment error [4].
At an ordinary multi-parent join, the child MUST be no more permissive than every parent in every required coordinate. For PIC authority:

figure.artwork: C(e) subset-of intersection of C(p), for every p in Pred(e)

section.t: A grant, authority composition, declassification, endorsement, or other non-conservative change MUST be represented as an explicit authorized relaxation. It MUST NOT be presented as an ordinary continuation.

section.name: Execution Integrity Coordinate
section.t: Execution integrity is an optional COSS coordinate describing which properties of the concrete execution a verifier has established. A profile may include properties such as the execution environment, measured workload, binding between that environment and the record-signing key, policy commitment, or transcript commitment. The coordinate is semantic and implementation-independent: an evidence format or project is not itself a coordinate.

An execution-integrity profile MUST define its state space, the order between states, the behaviors admitted at each state, the exact evidence required, the verifier and trust inputs, and the treatment of missing or unsupported evidence. It MUST distinguish producer claims from independently verified properties. Runtime attestation or a signature over an evidence envelope MUST NOT, by itself, be treated as proof that every claim inside the envelope is true.

One execution-integrity profile MAY use the relational construction of [6]: its state is a positive executor envelope rho, ordinary refinement requires rho(i+1) => rho(i), and admission requires sound evidence that the predecessor envelope holds for the current transition. Such a profile MUST use positive predicates unless it defines a sound treatment of negation, and missing evidence MUST NOT produce admission. This is one valid construction, not the mandatory representation of every execution-integrity coordinate. A profile based on attestation grades or another state space MUST independently define and justify its own order and admitted-behavior semantics.

TRACE is a candidate execution-evidence system for realizing such a profile [11]. A TRACE Trust Record can commit to the program or workload named by the producer, runtime, policy, data classification, tool transcript, build provenance, and transparency information. TRACE version 0.2 authenticates the producer's record but does not by itself establish the truth of each contained claim. Its runtime-evidence work is currently a non-normative proposal for a future version and defines candidate attestation grades and external platform-verifier inputs [12].

A future COSS-to-TRACE profile may use a TRACE record as occurrence evidence and may map independently verified TRACE runtime results into the execution-integrity coordinate. Such a profile MUST identify the exact TRACE version and revision and MUST define same-occurrence binding, the coordinate order, admission rules, predecessor representation, and failure semantics. Merely naming TRACE, carrying a TRACE signature, or asserting a runtime platform does not establish conformance to this specification or to an execution-integrity profile.

section.name: COSS Proof of Relationship and Proof of Continuity
section.t: PoP, PoR, and PoC answer different questions:

texttable.c: Does the presenter control a key or artifact?
Authenticates possession. It does not identify the causal occurrence.
Does this occurrence validly continue this specific predecessor on the shared causal graph?
Establishes the profile-defined causal edge. It does not by itself establish occurrence binding, coordinate refinement, or admission.
Does the represented execution preserve the selected COSS rules across every coordinate in K?
Composes accepted COSS PoR edges with ordinary coordinate refinement and separately authorized relaxation boundaries.

section.t: PoP MAY protect a COSS record or a referenced artifact, but PoP alone MUST NOT be accepted as COSS PoR or COSS PoC. A digest chain establishes artifact linkage only. It establishes COSS continuity only when the applicable profiles also validate the causal relationships and coordinate rules.

PoR_COSS(p, e) holds only when the Verifier establishes that CER(e) identifies the exact authenticated CER(p) as a predecessor and that the claimed edge is a valid causal continuation under the selected relationship profile. Profile-specific checks whose purpose is to witness that causal relation are part of its concrete PoR realization. Occurrence binding, coordinate-evidence validity, predecessor-state coherence, refinement, freshness, revocation, and admission remain separate checks even when all are required to accept a step. When PIC is in K, its authority-handoff relationship check contributes the PIC realization of the causal edge; that check alone is not a complete COSS step result.
For a trusted-policy-selected coordinate set K, define:

list.t: OccurrenceBind_COSS(e, K) to mean that the behavior and every required evidence item are bound to the occurrence represented by e;
PredCoherent_COSS(p, e, K) to mean that every coordinate-specific predecessor reference resolves to the corresponding coordinate state committed by the exact CER(p); and
EvidenceValid_COSS(e, K) to mean that each required coordinate state and its evidence are valid under that coordinate's profile and trust inputs.

section.t: For an ordinary edge, the accepted step condition is:

figure.artwork: Step_COSS^K(p, e) = PoR_COSS(p, e) AND OccurrenceBind_COSS(e, K) AND PredCoherent_COSS(p, e, K) AND EvidenceValid_COSS(e, K) AND sigma_j(e) <=_j sigma_j(p) for every j in K

section.t: At a join, this condition applies to every represented immediate predecessor. For an authorized relaxation, only the affected coordinate order checks are replaced by a separately verified relaxation rule. PoR, occurrence binding, predecessor coherence, evidence validity, and ordinary refinement of unaffected coordinates remain mandatory.

Projection of a successful COSS PoC to the PIC coordinate entails PIC PoC only on a path segment containing exclusively ordinary PIC transitions. At an authorized relaxation, the preceding authority bound does not continue across the relaxation; the ordinary bound restarts from the explicitly authorized resulting state [4]. A COSS PoC that contains such a boundary therefore MUST NOT be presented as one end-to-end PIC PoC across that boundary. Likewise, the PIC confused-deputy exclusion result applies only to request-to-effect paths that satisfy the paper's ordinary-segment premise, together with causal completeness and protected-effect mediation [4].
PIC PoC alone does not entail COSS PoC. Joint admission is a subsequent decision: Admit_COSS^K(e) additionally requires every coordinate in K to admit the committed behavior at the protected effect.
There is one predecessor graph. There is not an unrelated PIC chain, IFC chain, and execution-integrity chain later correlated by timestamp or actor name.

section.name: Evidence and Verification Results
section.t: A COSS Evidence Record is witness material. It carries or references the authenticated occurrence, predecessor, behavior, coordinate, and relaxation evidence on which a Verifier can operate. Possession, transport, signature validation, or schema validation of a record does not by itself establish COSS PoR or COSS PoC.
The Verifier derives separate results:

figure.artwork: PoR_COSS(p, e) = accepted or rejected PoC_COSS^K(e) = accepted or rejected Admit_COSS^K(e) = accepted or rejected for the committed behavior

section.t: A profile MAY define a serializable verifier-result object, but it MUST keep that result distinct from the evidence record. The result MUST identify the Verifier, trust inputs, exact coordinate set K, profile versions, evaluation time, exact record or graph evaluated, and the assurance established for every required coordinate. If a profile uses the labels full-continuity and artifact-linked, it MUST use them consistently with the PIC Prover and Verifier specification: an artifact-linked result establishes only the stated linkage properties and MUST NOT be presented as full semantic PoR or PoC. A full COSS continuity result requires full assurance for the causal relation and for every coordinate in K; an aggregate result MUST NOT hide a weaker required-coordinate result.

section.name: COSS Evidence Record
section.t: A COSS Evidence Record CER(e) is an authenticated commitment with the following logical fields:

texttable.c: The exact COSS evidence specification or profile version.
A commitment to the concrete execution occurrence.
An identifier or commitment for the trusted policy that selects required coordinates and verification rules.
Digest references to the exact authenticated predecessor records.
A commitment to the request, message, or protected effect being judged.
Typed references to occurrence, causal, or coordinate evidence.

For an authorized relaxation, the affected coordinates and commitments to the authorization source, authorization rule, exact input states, resulting states or bounds, scope, and applicable freshness evidence.

section.t: Every digest reference MUST identify the digest algorithm and the digest of the exact referenced bytes. The profile MUST define which bytes are hashed. A locator MAY accompany a digest but MUST NOT be trusted for identity or integrity.
An evidence entry declares one or more roles:

list.t: occurrence evidence describes what ran or which concrete request, message, or effect occurred;
causal evidence supports one or more claimed predecessor relationships; and
coordinate evidence supports a state, refinement, or admission result under a named coordinate profile.

section.t: One artifact MAY fulfill several roles. A runtime or provenance record is not automatically a security-state coordinate: it becomes coordinate evidence only under a profile that defines its state, order, admitted behavior, and verifier. For example, a TRACE record may be occurrence evidence without thereby making TRACE a coordinate; only an execution-integrity profile can assign independently verified TRACE results a coordinate state.

A coordinate-evidence entry MUST identify its coordinate and exact profile version. It MUST also carry or commit to the coordinate state established for the occurrence and reference the evidence from which that result is verified. The state MAY remain selectively disclosed if the profile supplies a proof sufficient for refinement and admission.

If coordinate evidence carries its own predecessor identifier or predecessor-state commitment, the profile MUST define how it is resolved. For every claimed edge p -> e, that reference MUST identify the state of the same coordinate committed by the exact authenticated CER(p). At a multi-parent join, the check applies separately to the coordinate state associated with every applicable parent. A valid coordinate artifact referring to another predecessor MUST be rejected rather than correlated by time, actor, workflow, or similar metadata.

A root record has no predecessors. An ordinary or authorized-relaxation record has one or more distinct predecessors. The resolved predecessor relation MUST be acyclic. A profile MUST NOT infer a missing predecessor from physical time or list order.

section.name: Same-Occurrence Binding
section.t: Every required evidence entry MUST be bound to the record's occurrence. A profile MAY establish this in either of two ways:

list.t: the evidence artifact directly commits to the same occurrence; or
a trusted handoff boundary authenticates one record that commits together to the occurrence, its predecessor records, and the exact evidence-artifact digests.

section.t: The boundary-witnessed checkpoint kappa = (B, m, sigma) of [6] is one possible realization of the second method; it is not the only permitted realization. A profile using that construction MUST state how it discharges the applicable witness assumptions, including cryptographic unforgeability and binding, boundary protocol compliance, sound observation of the consumed handoff, sound executor-profile and relational evidence, replay or single-consumption control, and root validity.

The base CER has no mandatory top-level freshness field. A profile MUST nevertheless define freshness and replay semantics and MUST bind any nonce, challenge, sequence, validity interval, consumption marker, or equivalent evidence needed by those semantics. A unique occurrence commitment or an executed-versus-bound comparison does not by itself establish freshness or prevent replay.

Association performed later from timestamps, actor identifiers, workflow labels, or separately valid artifacts is insufficient. The binding MUST prevent an implementation from pairing valid PIC evidence from one execution with valid IFC or runtime evidence from another.

section.name: Authorized Relaxation Evidence
section.t: An authorized relaxation MUST identify the authority that approves the non-conservative transition. That authority MAY be a trust anchor or a delegated authority whose authorization path terminates at a trust anchor accepted under the Verifier's local policy. The authorization MUST be authenticated and MUST bind:

list.t: the applicable policy and authorization rule;
the exact predecessor records and affected input coordinate states;
the occurrence and behavior for which the relaxation is authorized;
every coordinate allowed to change;
the resulting coordinate states or an enforceable bound on them;
the authorization scope and any required freshness or replay evidence; and
any conditions that the receiving boundary must enforce.

section.t: The resulting state of each affected coordinate MUST satisfy the bound or rule explicitly granted by the relaxation authorization. This is a coordinate-profile obligation: COSS does not impose one cross-coordinate order between an authorizer's PIC authority and an IFC, geographic, or execution-integrity state. For PIC grants or authority composition, the applicable profile MUST define the authority source and prove that the resulting authority does not exceed the grant or composition bound supplied by that source. For declassification or another coordinate-specific relaxation, the applicable profile MUST define the corresponding authorization semantics.

A signature by a trusted key authenticates the authorization object; it does not by itself prove that the signer was authorized for this rule, that the object applies to these inputs and this occurrence, or that the resulting state satisfies the authorized bound. The Verifier MUST establish all of those properties before accepting the relaxation.

section.name: References Are Not Validation
section.t: An authenticated digest reference proves that the signer committed to exact artifact bytes. It does not prove that:

list.t: the referenced statement is true;
its issuer is trusted for the claimed role;
the artifact establishes PoR;
its coordinate state is correctly ordered; or
the behavior is admitted.

section.t: Each referenced artifact MUST therefore be resolved, integrity-checked, and independently validated by the verifier required by its declared profile. An unavailable required artifact causes verification to fail unless the selected profile defines an equivalent self-contained proof.

section.name: Illustrative Record
section.t: The following JSON is illustrative and is not a wire format or a registry of identifier strings:

The record binds three external artifacts to one mail-send occurrence. It does not ask the execution-evidence system to compute PIC attenuation, and it does not ask PIC to decide IFC or execution integrity. Dave validates each required profile and then applies the joint admission rule.

section.name: Minimal Integration Contract
section.t: An execution-evidence system can support COSS Evidence Records without implementing PIC or IFC internally. Its profile needs to provide:

list.t: an authenticated record for the concrete occurrence and behavior;
digest references that form the represented predecessor graph;
typed digest references to external coordinate evidence;
same-occurrence binding for those references;
coordinate-specific predecessor references that resolve to the corresponding states in the exact predecessor CERs;
a way for the receiving verifier to invoke, or validate the result of, each required coordinate verifier; and
for a non-conservative transition, separately authenticated relaxation evidence bound to its exact inputs and resulting bounds.

section.t: The authority intersection remains a PIC operation. IFC admission remains an IFC operation. The execution-evidence system records and binds the facts on which those independent decisions rely.

section.name: Verification
section.t: A conformant verifier MUST perform the following checks in order:

list.t: Record validation. Parse the record under the selected profile; reject unsupported versions, malformed fields, duplicate coordinate identifiers not explicitly allowed by profile, and unsafe resource consumption.
Record authenticity. Validate the record's integrity, authenticating mechanism, trust anchor, algorithm policy, and profile-defined freshness or replay rules.

Policy selection. Resolve the policy under local trusted configuration and determine the required coordinates, evidence profiles, and verification rules. The producer MUST NOT be able to select a weaker policy for the effect.
Occurrence and behavior binding. Recompute or otherwise validate the commitments to the concrete request, message, or effect being judged.
Reference integrity. Resolve every required artifact and verify its digest over the profile-defined exact bytes.
Evidence validity. Apply the verifier and trust policy declared by every required evidence profile. A reference signature is not a substitute for this step.

Causal validity. Validate that predecessor references are distinct, the resolved graph is acyclic, the declared predecessor set is complete under the selected profile, and the required PoR evidence is valid. Root, ordinary linear, ordinary join, and authorized-relaxation records MUST NOT be confused.

Coordinate-predecessor coherence. For every coordinate-specific predecessor reference, verify that it resolves to the corresponding coordinate state committed by the exact predecessor CER. At a join, perform this check independently for every applicable parent.

Coordinate continuity. For an ordinary record, verify that every coordinate in K is no more permissive than every applicable predecessor under that coordinate's declared order. If a profile performs a heterogeneous translation, verify its required translation and semantic-soundness conditions.

Relaxation authorization. For an authorized relaxation, authenticate the authorization source to a locally accepted trust anchor; verify its delegated authority when applicable; verify the bound policy, inputs, occurrence, behavior, affected coordinates, resulting states or bounds, scope, and freshness; and enforce the coordinate-specific relaxation rule. Unaffected coordinates remain subject to ordinary continuity.
Joint admission. Before a protected effect, verify that every coordinate in K admits the committed behavior. Any required rejection rejects the effect.

Result construction. Bind the verdict to the exact record or graph, K, profile versions, trust inputs, evaluation time, and per-coordinate assurance. Do not aggregate an artifact-linked required-coordinate result into a full COSS continuity claim.

section.t: An implementation MUST fail closed when a required coordinate, artifact, verifier, causal edge, or binding cannot be established. It MUST NOT silently reduce a multi-coordinate decision to the coordinates it happens to understand.

section.name: Rejected Ordinary Path
section.t: For Carol's proposed mail effect, assume the evidence establishes:

figure.artwork: PIC authority: send-email is present IFC provenance: the bytes depend on Alice's HIGH documents execution integrity: the required occurrence properties are independently established destination policy: external email is LOW causal binding: all results refer to this exact send occurrence

section.t: The authority coordinate admits send-email. The IFC coordinate rejects the HIGH -> LOW flow. Dave therefore rejects the effect. PIC does not claim that Carol is physically unable to copy or transmit bytes through an unmediated path; it establishes that such an effect is not a valid admitted continuation. The claimed protection requires the mail effect to pass through Dave or another complete mediation boundary.

section.name: Accepted DLP Path
section.t: Suppose Carol does not initially hold send-email. Alice's read-for-verification continuity and Bob's send-email continuity arrive as separate inputs. For this example, Dave's domain trusts a composition authority P, either directly as a trust anchor or through a validated delegation chain. Policy permits P to authorize their composition only for a DLP-mediated mail occurrence. P signs an authorization that binds the exact Alice and Bob predecessor CERs, Carol's DLP occurrence, the applicable policy, the resulting PIC authority bound, the output destination, scope, and freshness evidence. That union is not an ordinary join. It MUST be represented as an explicit authorized composition whose COSS record has transition class authorized-relaxation.
Carol then evaluates the exact candidate output under the selected DLP or IFC profile. Two cases are distinct:

list.t: If the verified output state already admits flow to the destination, no IFC relaxation is needed.

If the output is derived from HIGH input and is released or sanitized for a LOW destination, the change MUST be an explicit authorized declassification. Its evidence MUST bind the input, exact output bytes, applicable policy, and declassification authorization.

section.t: The evidence graph makes both possible security boundaries visible:

figure.artwork: Alice read ----\ > [authorized composition] --> Carol DLP Bob send -----/ | P authorization ------------------------------>| | verifies output Trent data ----------------------------------->| v [declassification if needed] | v Dave mail

section.t: The record presented to Dave binds at least:

figure.artwork: behavior: digest of destination, message, and exact output bytes predecessor: digest of the authenticated predecessor record PIC coordinate evidence: digest of the authorized composition and authority state IFC coordinate evidence: digest of the DLP/IFC result for the exact output relaxation evidence: digest of P's authorization and any required declassification occurrence evidence: digest of the execution evidence for this handoff

section.t: Dave accepts only if P chains to an accepted trust anchor, P is authorized for the bound composition rule, the resulting PIC state stays within the signed composition bound and admits send-email, the DLP or IFC result admits the exact output and destination, any required declassification is authorized, and every item is bound to the same occurrence. Without the required composition or declassification evidence, valid evidence in another coordinate does not repair the missing rule.

section.name: Conformance
section.t: A COSS Evidence Producer conforms to this specification when it creates authenticated records that bind the occurrence, policy, predecessors, behavior, evidence references, and transition class as required above.

A COSS Evidence Verifier conforms when it implements the ordered verification procedure, validates every required external profile independently, reports K and per-coordinate assurance, and fails closed on missing or unsupported required evidence.

A COSS Evidence Profile conforms when it defines the concrete serialization, authenticating mechanism, exact-byte digest rules, occurrence and behavior commitments, coordinate identifiers, semantically monotone coordinate orders, predecessor-state coherence, heterogeneous translations when used, evidence verifiers, freshness rules, authorized-relaxation rules, assurance semantics, and the required-coordinate policy needed to realize this specification.
Conformance to this document does not imply conformance to PIC, an IFC system, or any referenced evidence system. Those claims require independent conformance to the corresponding specifications.

section.name: Origins, Authorship, and Historical Record
section.t: This section is informative.

The Provenance Identity Continuity (PIC) Model was originally developed by Nicola Gallo as a formal framework for reasoning about causal authority propagation across distributed execution. Its development introduced Proof of Relationship (PoR), Proof of Continuity (PoC), authority non-expansion, relational attenuation, and event-level causal provenance as connected parts of the framework. COSS generalizes the carried security state from authority to a finite product of ordered security coordinates on the same causal occurrence. The PIC Specifications translate those formal results into technical requirements and are published and maintained by Nitro Agility S.r.l. as Specification Steward.

The name COSS abbreviates Causally Ordered Security-State. “Causally Ordered” identifies the single causal partial order shared by all represented security facts; “Security-State” identifies the product of ordered security coordinates carried on that structure. The name records how COSS was obtained from PIC: PIC remains the authority-continuity coordinate, while additional security-state coordinates are added without introducing a separate temporal or causal axis.

section.t: The publicly verifiable research record is:

list.t: 1 December 2025 — initial public PIC Model working paper. PIC Model — Provenance Identity Continuity for Distributed Execution Systems, Zenodo record 17777421 [9]. That archived draft is retained for historical reference and is not an implementation specification.
5 December 2025 — authority-propagation analysis. Authority Propagation Models: PoP vs PoC and the Confused Deputy Problem, Zenodo record 17833000 [8].

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: The primary threat addressed by this document is evidence mix-and-match: combining valid evidence from different occurrences so that it appears to justify one effect. Same-occurrence binding and exact predecessor references are REQUIRED to prevent that substitution.

A digest authenticates bytes only through a separately trusted signature or channel and says nothing by itself about semantic truth. Weak, deprecated, ambiguous, or incorrectly canonicalized digest inputs can defeat the binding. Profiles MUST define exact-byte hashing and algorithm-agility policy.

Omitting a coordinate can change a security verdict. Required coordinates MUST therefore be selected by trusted policy, not by the producer. Unknown required coordinates and unavailable required evidence MUST fail closed.

Causal evidence can be incomplete or false. Claims that depend on complete causal ancestry additionally require sound causal evidence, representation of every in-scope cause, and mediation of every protected effect. This specification cannot protect causes or effects omitted from the modeled and mediated execution.
Replay, fan-out, freshness, revocation, trust-anchor compromise, and equivocation remain profile and deployment concerns. A valid historical record is not automatically valid for a new occurrence.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: Cross-coordinate evidence can expose principals, software identities, data classifications, locations, causal relationships, and stable execution identifiers. Profiles SHOULD use commitments, selective disclosure, scoped identifiers, and minimum necessary retention while preserving the evidence needed for the claimed security property. Digest references can still enable correlation when the same artifact is reused across domains.

section.t: This section is informative.

list.t: 0.2 — 26 October 2026. Initial public draft defining the COSS Evidence Record; protocol-neutral same-occurrence binding of PIC, IFC, execution-integrity, and other coordinate evidence; COSS PoR and PoC over a trusted-policy-selected coordinate set; ordinary-segment and authorized-relaxation semantics; coordinate predecessor coherence; per-coordinate assurance; optional TRACE integration; and the planned COSS Prover and Verifier and COSS-to-TRACE companion specifications without making them current dependencies.
